content: Adults diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes are advised to participate in at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week or alternatively, 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic exercise per week. Additionally, they should incorporate resistance training exercises into their routine at least three times per week. It is recommended that individuals with diabetes perform muscle-strengthening and bone-strengthening exercises on at least two to three days per week. For adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, resistance training should be performed two to three times per week on nonconsecutive days to allow for adequate recovery between sessions. Older adults with diabetes are encouraged to engage in flexibility and balance training, such as yoga or tai chi, two to three times per week. These activities are beneficial for improving flexibility, muscle strength, and balance, which are critical for maintaining physical function and reducing the risk of falls. All individuals with diabetes should undergo an assessment of their baseline physical activity levels, including the amount of time spent in sedentary behaviors such as sitting or lying down. For those who do not currently meet recommended physical activity guidelines, it is important to encourage an increase in physical activity. Suggested activities include walking, yoga, housework, gardening, swimming, and dancing, with the goal of exceeding their baseline activity levels.
